description: Five visitor-accessible rounds around Lake Tahoe: the celebrity-tournament stage at Edgewood Tahoe, the Nicklaus test at Old Greenwood, the home-free mountain golf at Coyote Moon, the Jacobsen layout at Gray's Crossing, and the classic public course on the South Shore.
intro: Lake Tahoe is one of the few places where you can play a PGA Tour venue, a celebrity-championship stage, and a quiet locals' favorite all in the same long weekend — and every one of them is open to visitors. The catch is the calendar: at more than 6,000 feet, the season runs roughly late spring through October, so a Tahoe golf trip is a summer and early-fall play. Base yourself in Truckee for the north-shore courses or in South Lake Tahoe for the south shore, and remember the altitude — the ball flies noticeably farther up here, so club down and enjoy the extra distance.

sections.heading: 1. Edgewood Tahoe Golf Course, Stateline
paragraphs: The most famous round in Tahoe is also the one every golf fan has already seen on television. Edgewood Tahoe sits right on the lake's south shore in Stateline, Nevada, a George Fazio design from 1968 that was later renovated by his nephew Tom Fazio. It has hosted the American Century Championship — the celebrity golf tournament broadcast on NBC every July — since 1991, and its championship pedigree runs deeper: the course hosted the USGA's U.S. Amateur Public Links Championship in 1980 and the U.S. Senior Open in 1985, and Golf Digest has regularly named it one of America's 100 greatest public courses. The par-72 layout stretches to 7,529 yards from the back tees, with the lake in view and the High Sierra as the backdrop.

Edgewood is a public course, and public tee times can be booked 60 days in advance through the resort — plan around that window, because summer mornings go fast. The season is short, roughly mid-May to mid-October, and the course closes entirely in winter, so book a summer trip rather than hoping for a shoulder-season round. Play it as the centerpiece of a South Lake Tahoe stay: it is minutes from the south-shore casino hotels, and the closing stretch along the lake is the round you will remember. Avoid tournament week in July unless you are there to watch — the course is closed to public play while the celebrities are in town.

sections.heading: 2. Old Greenwood Golf Course, Truckee
paragraphs: If Edgewood is Tahoe's showpiece, Old Greenwood is its serious golf test. The Jack Nicklaus Signature course in Truckee opened in 2004, routed through 600 acres of towering pines on the north side of the lake, and it plays every bit of its 7,518 yards at par 72. Nicklaus Signature is the highest level of personal attention the Golden Bear gives a design, and it shows in the strategic bunkering and the big, demanding greens. The course has hosted the PGA Tour's Barracuda Championship, and Golf Digest ranked it among America's finest new upscale public courses when it opened. The sixth hole is the signature: a risk-reward par 5 that tempts you to go for it in two. Even the tee system is distinctive — tees are named by trees, from 1 Tree through 4 Trees, rather than by color.

Old Greenwood is semi-private, but public tee times are bookable online, so visitors can get on — just book well ahead in peak summer, when Tahoe Mountain Club members and stay-and-play guests get preferred access. It pairs naturally with the other Truckee courses on this list: base yourself in Truckee for two or three nights and play Old Greenwood as your hardest round, ideally on a day when you are fresh. The course is cart-path-only in places and the greens are quick, so bring your best putting stroke and allow extra time between rounds.

sections.heading: 3. Coyote Moon Golf Course, Truckee
paragraphs: Coyote Moon is the purest mountain-golf experience in Truckee, and the easiest to love. Designed by former PGA Tour pro Brad Bell and opened in 2000, the public par-72 course plays 7,177 yards through pine forest and high meadow at the north end of the Tahoe basin — and it has one feature almost no modern course can claim: not a single home lines any fairway, so every view is uninterrupted Sierra scenery. The routing climbs and falls through the forest with the kind of elevation changes that make club selection an adventure, and regulars call the 13th hole the best par 3 in all of Lake Tahoe.

Coyote Moon is the best value play on a Truckee trip and the ideal second round after the bigger-ticket Old Greenwood or Gray's Crossing. Because it is fully public with online booking, it is also the easiest to fit into a flexible itinerary — use it as your arrival-day round or as the relaxed morning before a drive home. Wildlife is a real part of the round here, with bears and coyotes occasionally spotted on the course, so keep your distance and enjoy the show. Book a morning tee time for the calmest conditions; the afternoons can bring the mountain wind.

sections.heading: 4. Gray's Crossing Golf Course, Truckee
paragraphs: Gray's Crossing is the modern complement to Old Greenwood, a few minutes away in Truckee and part of the same Tahoe Mountain Club family. Designed by Peter Jacobsen and Jim Hardy and opened in 2007, the par-72 course plays 7,466 yards from the back tees through lodgepole and Jeffrey pines, with native grasses, wetlands, and Mount Rose as the backdrop. It began life as a private club and is now open to everyone, which explains the private-club feel — fast greens, tournament-like conditioning, and an expert caddie program. The finishing hole is the talking point: a par 5 with double fairways divided by a riot of wildflowers. The course is also an Audubon International Gold Signature Sanctuary, only the second golf course in California to earn that certification.

Gray's Crossing and Old Greenwood are the natural one-two punch of a Truckee golf weekend, and playing them back to back shows off two very different Nicklaus-versus-Jacobsen philosophies on the same mountain terrain. Peak-season tee times book 30 or more days out, so lock in your dates early, especially for weekend slots. Finish at PJ's Bar and Grill, the course's 19th hole overlooking the 18th green, for the post-round debrief — it is one of the best patios in Truckee golf.

sections.heading: 5. Lake Tahoe Golf Course, South Lake Tahoe
paragraphs: The South Shore's premier public course is also its most old-school. Lake Tahoe Golf Course opened in 1959, a William Bell Jr. design set in a grassy mountain meadow at 6,260 feet, with the Upper Truckee River winding through the layout and 360-degree Sierra Nevada views from nearly every hole. The par-71 course plays 6,683 yards — shorter than the Truckee championship tests, but no pushover: the flat meadow setting demands accurate iron play rather than brute length, and the river comes into play more than you would expect. It is also the Tahoe Basin's only certified Audubon Cooperative Sanctuary golf course, a quiet credential that fits a layout that has always felt more like a walk in the meadow than a resort production.

This is the round to book when you want classic, affordable Tahoe golf without the premium-resort production around it — the locals' favorite on the South Shore, minutes from Highway 50 near Meyers. It pairs perfectly with Edgewood as a South Lake Tahoe two-day: play the big-stage round at Edgewood one day and the relaxed meadow round here the next. The course is open seasonally, roughly mid-April through late October, so check availability before you travel, and note that the facility stays busy year-round with events — book your tee time ahead rather than counting on a walk-up.
